analysis: Examined base_text lines 1-2004 of fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json, which are golden prompt-contract test vectors (request_body, provider_body, template_input, plan with prompt_contract_id/block chain hashes, token_ids) for the EigenLabs/Qwen3.8-27B-4bit-mtp model. The changed ranges (base 3024-4824, 43813-54138; head 3020-54088) all fall outside these units. The patch excerpt shows a fixture case gaining additional_context.enable_thinking=false in template_input, with a reduced prompt_token_count (803->767), new block chain hashes and fewer token_ids. This reflects a template-rendering contract change (thinking prefix omitted), not a change to security controls. The relevant threat context is T-041 (prefix-cache cross-tenant sharing and HMAC-keyed cache at-rest artifacts) and TB-007. Chain hashes in fixtures are deterministic test expectations, and the fixture uses scope_id 'fixture-scope'. No secrets appear in the visible units: only public token IDs and hashes of fixture text. Integration should confirm that the code consuming enable_thinking (provider template rendering and coordinator prompt planning) keeps cache scope/tenant isolation in block hashing. It should also confirm that additional_context is not an unvalidated consumer-controlled field that could desynchronize coordinator routing plans from provider rendering. That desynchronization would be a cache-routing correctness or timing concern under T-041. The implementing code is not in these units, so this remains a question rather than a finding.
